# `code` operations

The exact fields each `code.*` operation takes and returns.

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/codegen/docs_reference.py` from the op registry; edit the models, not this page. -->

Every op is `POST /v1/<op>` over HTTP and the MCP tool `loom_<op>`. The identity fields (`org`, `namespace`, `agent`, `user_id`, `session_id`) are filled from the token and the MCP session when a transport can; see [identities and namespaces](../../concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md). The [operations index](../operations.md) explains role, kind and the MCP `all` listing. Unknown input fields are served and named in `ignored_args`.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

## `code.ask`

Ask a QUESTION about this codebase and get a grounded answer with [file:line] citations — 'how does TTL drop old rows', 'where is the memory limit enforced'.

`POST /v1/code.ask` · MCP `loom_code_ask` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `question` | `str` | required | The question to answer about the indexed code (grounded on a code.search of it). |
| `synthesize` | `bool` | `True` | False = retrieval-only (agent synthesizes); True = grounded server-side answer with citations, memoized across agents and invalidated when any cited file changes at merge. |
| `rerank` | `str` | `''` | Reranker for the retrieval: "" = the deployment default (LOOM_CODE_SEARCH_RERANK_DEFAULT), "none" = off for this request, "builtin:openai" / "builtin:cohere", or the name of an endpoint in LOOM_RERANK_ENDPOINTS_JSON (not a URL). |
| `no_cache` | `bool` | `False` | Skip the cache lookup and synthesize fresh (the fresh answer still refreshes the cache entry). |
| `token_budget` | `int \| None` | `None` | Retrieval context handed to synthesis, in tokens. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `answer` | `str` | The grounded answer text; "" on an abstain or when synthesize=false. |
| `citations` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | The units the answer used (or was shown when none is cited): {path, start_line, end_line, symbol, unit_id} each; the retrieved units when synthesize=false. |
| `source` | `Literal['cached', 'synthesized', 'abstained']` | cached = served from the answer cache \| synthesized = answered now (or retrieval-only when synthesize=false) \| abstained = no grounded answer (`abstain_reason` says why). |
| `cache_similarity` | `float` | Cosine between this question and the served cached question; 0.0 unless source=cached. |
| `cache` | `str` | What the answer cache did. hit (a cached answer whose key, identifiers and files all matched) \| miss \| stale (the nearest entry's files, prompt version or age invalidated it) \| guarded (the nearest cached question names different… |
| `cache_saved_ms` | `int` | On a served entry: the synthesis wall (ms) and upstream cost (USD) the entry recorded when it was written, i.e. what this call did not pay. |
| `cache_saved_usd` | `float` | Upstream LLM cost in USD the served cache entry recorded; 0.0 when nothing was served. |
| `abstain` | `bool` | true when no grounded answer is returned; `abstain_reason` says why. |
| `abstain_reason` | `str` | Why it abstained (no strong match, off-repository question, ...); "" otherwise. |
| `retrieval_confidence` | `float` | The underlying code.search's calibrated confidence (0-1); 0.0 when it did not run. |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated tokens of the answer text (characters / 4); 0 when there is no answer. |
| `context_tokens` | `int` | Retrieval context (tokens) the synthesis was grounded on; 0 for cached hits and abstains. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of the loom.code_search_trace row the server writes for this call. |
| `as_of` | `dict[str, Any]` | Provenance + freshness: branch, commit, indexed_at, lag_commits (int, -1 unknown), stale (bool: lag > LOOM_CODE_STALE_AFTER_COMMITS). |

## `code.backport_gap`

Which release branches still carry the bug this fix removed, and the exact PR to cherry-pick there?

`POST /v1/code.backport_gap` · MCP `loom_code_backport_gap` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | The merged trunk fix to check; 0 = take it from `issue_number`. |
| `issue_number` | `int` | `0` | An issue the fix closes: the tracker graph's `fixes` edges name the PR. |
| `branches` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Release branches to check, as namespaces or versions (`26.4`), at most 8; empty = every configured release branch of the repository the caller can read. |
| `max_symbols` | `int` | `8` | At most this many touched functions (1–8) are looked up on each branch. |
| `exact` | `bool` | `False` | Hunk-level presence per branch, on request (one chunk read per branch and the fix's diff sections from the tracker record) |
| `history` | `bool` | `False` | For the branches the lines leave undecided, the fix's removed lines on the branch's own history in the mirror (git grep at the tip, git log -S over the first-parent history; at most 3 lines, 2 s per branch) — the pre-image at the tip is… |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skipped_branches` | `list[dict[str, str]]` | Configured release branches this caller cannot read, skipped (never silently): [{namespace, reason}]. |
| `verdict` | `str` | gap \| pending \| covered \| not_affected \| unknown — the worst branch's word |
| `causes` | `list[str]` | tracker_unbound \| tracker_unavailable \| fix_not_found \| no_fix \| no_branches \| per-branch unknown reasons (deadline, no_index, no_branch_version, …) |
| `fix` | `dict[str, Any]` | {pr_number, title, url, base_branch, minor_version, merged_at, merge_sha, changelog_category, src_components, files, hunk_contexts, ledger} plus, under `exact`, `patch: {files, hunks, added, removed, symbols}` |
| `issue` | `dict[str, Any]` | from issue_number: {number, title, affected_versions, fix_versions, fixed_by} |
| `fixes` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | every PR the issue's `fixes` edges name, with merged / backport flags |
| `symbols` | `list[str]` | the touched functions presence was tested with (from the hunk headers) |
| `files` | `list[str]` | the fix's source files (the file leg when no hunk named a function) |
| `branches` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | one row per branch, gaps first, newest branch first: {namespace, branch, verdict, epistemic exact\|lower_bound, basis, reason, backport, presence, cherry_pick {pr_number, merge_sha}, evidence [...]}; under `exact`, presence.patch = {mode… |
| `summary` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | verdict → [branch versions] |
| `fix_candidate` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | When no `fixes` edge named a trunk PR, the link pass's top candidate above LOOM_TRACKER_LINKS_MIN_SCORE stood in as the fix ({pr_number, score, rank, why, features, …, epistemic candidate}) and `fix.source` reads `candidate`; absent… |
| `tracker_namespace` | `str` | The tracker namespace bound to the trunk namespace that was read; "" when none is bound. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when a tracker is bound but its read failed. |
| `ms` | `int` | Wall time of the whole read, in milliseconds. |
| `stage_ms` | `dict[str, int]` | {fix: ms of the record + ledger stage, presence: ms of the presence stage, patch: ms of the hunk-level stage (under `exact` only)} |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.backport_gaps`

The set-wide backport report: which merged fixes labelled for backport does a release branch still owe?

`POST /v1/code.backport_gaps` · MCP `loom_code_backport_gaps` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `branch` | `str` | `''` | One release branch, as a namespace or a version (`26.6`); "" = every configured release branch the caller can read. |
| `wanted_only` | `bool` | `True` | Keep only the fixes labelled for backport; false also returns unlabelled fixes. |
| `days` | `int` | `90` | Only fixes merged in the last this many days (1–365). |
| `limit` | `int` | `500` | At most this many rows (1–5000). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skipped_branches` | `list[dict[str, str]]` | Configured release branches this caller cannot read, skipped (never silently): [{namespace, reason}]. |
| `branch` | `str` | the branch asked for ('' = every configured release branch) |
| `branch_namespace` | `str` | The namespace of the branch asked for; "" when every branch was read. |
| `branches` | `list[str]` | the release-branch namespaces the rows cover, newest first |
| `rows` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | one row per (fix, branch), gaps first, wanted-on-this-branch first, newest fix first: {pr_number, title, merged_at, minor_version, branch, branch_namespace, verdict, epistemic, basis, reason, cherry_pick {pr_number, merge_sha}… |
| `counts` | `dict[str, int]` | verdict → rows returned |
| `counts_by_branch` | `dict[str, dict[str, int]]` | branch version → verdict → rows |
| `fixes` | `int` | How many distinct fixes the returned rows cover. |
| `wanted_only` | `bool` | Echo of the request's `wanted_only`. |
| `since` | `str` | The merge-time lower bound applied (ISO-8601 UTC): now minus `days`. |
| `computed` | `dict[str, Any]` | the table's state for this trunk: {fixes, rows, first_computed, last_computed} |
| `stale` | `bool` | no pass has written this trunk yet, or the last pass is older than two intervals |
| `ms` | `int` | Wall time of the read, in milliseconds. |

## `code.bisect_candidates`

Rank PRs that may have introduced a bug; Loom does not test or reproduce it.

`POST /v1/code.bisect_candidates` · MCP `loom_code_bisect_candidates` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `symbols` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Crashing frames from the stack trace (qualified symbol names, at most 12); the code index resolves them to files, and their specific bare names rank the diffs. |
| `paths` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Repo-relative source paths to scan (at most 20), beside the frames' files. |
| `patterns` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Greppable literals from the report (an error code, an identifier in the message, a setting name); with `issue_number` they are also derived from the issue's text. |
| `issue_number` | `int` | `0` | A tracker issue number: Loom reads but does not verify its previously recorded triage observations for the release range, its text for patterns, and its `caused_by` / `fixes` edges for the named culprit and fix. 0 = none. |
| `text` | `str` | `''` | The report's own words (title, body, error) when there is no tracker issue to read them from — they feed the fusion's vector and lexical legs and the suspects the report names. |
| `rerank` | `bool` | `False` | One LLM call reranks the fused top 20 (+~2 s); a weak fused top reranks without asking |
| `deadline_ms` | `int \| None` | `None` | Answer within this many milliseconds with the best candidates found so far. |
| `fix_pr` | `int` | `0` | The PR that fixed the regression, when one exists — its rewritten lines, blamed at its parent, name the change that broke them. |
| `bad_version` | `str` | `''` | The first release on which the caller or an upstream test observed the bug (`26.3`, or a full version cut to its minor); Loom does not test it, and the value wins over the issue's `reproduces_on`. "" = from the issue. |
| `before` | `str` | `''` | The inclusive upper bound of an approximate merge-time investigation window when release observations are unavailable; it narrows candidate history and does not mean Loom reproduced the bug. |
| `after` | `str` | `''` | Optional lower bound of the merge-time window (ISO-8601); must be earlier than `before`. |
| `bad_sha` | `str` | `''` | A commit (hex) whose commit time on the code mirror becomes `before` when `before` is unset; a sha the mirror lacks is refused with `BAD_SHA`. |
| `good_version` | `str` | `''` | The newest release that the caller or an upstream test observed as clean; Loom does not test it, and the value wins over the issue's `clean_on`. "" = from the issue, or a lookback from `bad_version`. |
| `widen_to_directories` | `bool` | `True` | widen the candidate set from the frames' files to their directories when frames or patterns can rank within it |
| `wideners` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | What may bound the scan when no frame resolves to a file — `patterns` (the window's diffs carrying the issue's rarest identifiers), `component` (the directories the issue's component touches), `fix_candidate` (the fix's own files: the… |
| `rescan` | `bool` | `False` | Run the scan even when the record already names the culprit (an introducing commit or a `caused_by` edge) — to check a pin; `introduced_commit` / `named_by_graph` still say what the record holds |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many candidates (1–25). |
| `marks` | `bool` | `True` | Marks on the candidates (backport, revert, reverted, re-land, whitespace / rename-only, touches_symbol, named); false returns the ranked candidate dicts unmarked |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `str` | candidates \| no_candidates \| already_bisected \| graph_named \| unknown |
| `candidates_from` | `str` | Where the candidates came from — `tracker` (its PR diff scan), `code_history` (loom's own PR ledger of the repository, when no tracker is linked or it holds no changed files), or `none` |
| `causes` | `list[str]` | Why the answer is thin or empty: tracker_unbound \| tracker_unavailable \| no_failing_version \| no_resolved_paths \| introduced_commit_known \| caused_by_edge. |
| `epistemic` | `str` | always lower_bound: the upstream file list and the diff text are what was searched; an empty answer excludes nothing |
| `candidates` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | {pr_number, title, author, merged_at, minor_version, matched_paths, matched_symbols, matched_patterns, added_patterns, kind change\|meta, has_test, url, score, merge_commit_sha, merge_sha_source stored\|mirror\|"", named_by?}; with `marks`… |
| `marks` | `dict[str, Any]` | what the marks stage did: {status ok\|skipped\|ledger_failed, git_calls, demoted, promoted, relands} |
| `named_by_graph` | `list[int]` | PR numbers the tracker graph's `caused_by` edges name for the issue; when set, the candidates are these and no scan ran |
| `fix_blame` | `dict[str, Any]` | What blaming the fix's rewritten lines found — the fix, its parent, the ranges blamed and the PRs they name; absent without a fix |
| `fusion` | `dict[str, Any]` | What the fusion read — {window_prs, signals: {name: count}, suspects: {named, mentioned}, rerank?}; each fused candidate carries `why` (the signals that ranked it in their top 10); absent when fusion did not run. |
| `patterns` | `list[str]` | the greppable literals the ranking used (given ∪ derived from the issue) |
| `pattern_weights` | `dict[str, float]` | IDF over the issue corpus per pattern — what each is worth in the ranking; absent when the vocabulary was not read |
| `scope` | `str` | file \| directory \| patterns — how wide the candidate set was drawn |
| `widened_by` | `list[str]` | Which frameless wideners bounded the scan — patterns \| component \| fix_candidate — in the order they applied; absent when a frame or a path resolved |
| `dupcheck_fix` | `dict[str, Any]` | With no fix_pr and no issue, the duplicate check matched the report to a reported issue whose linked merged fix became fix_pr — {issue, fix_pr, match: duplicate, namespace}; absent otherwise |
| `component` | `str` | the issue's QA component and the directories it widened the scan to |
| `component_dirs` | `list[str]` | The directories the issue's component widened the scan to; absent when none did. |
| `dropped_after_report` | `int` | Scanned PRs merged AFTER the issue was opened — the fix, or nothing — left out of the list; absent when none was |
| `versions_searched` | `list[str]` | The release minors whose PRs were scanned; empty when a time window bounded it. |
| `bad_version` | `str` | The failing release the range used (given, else the issue's); "" when unknown. |
| `good_version` | `str` | The clean release the range used (given, else the issue's); "" when unknown. |
| `window` | `str` | clean_to_bad_plus_slack \| lookback_from_bad \| master_after_clean — how the release range was drawn |
| `hub_paths_dropped` | `list[str]` | hub files (Settings.cpp, CMake, docs, …) left out of the file filter |
| `resolved` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{symbol, paths}] — what the code index resolved each frame to |
| `paths` | `list[str]` | The files the scan filtered on: fix files, given paths, the frames' files and the widening's, with hub files removed. |
| `frames` | `list[str]` | The bare frame names the diffs were ranked by: distinct, at least 6 characters, generic names dropped. |
| `issue` | `dict[str, Any]` | the issue's QA fact, as the tracker serves it, when issue_number was given |
| `introduced_commit` | `str` | The introducing commit the issue record holds; "" when none. |
| `fix_candidate` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | The issue's probable fix from the link pass when no `caused_by` edge and no introducing commit exist (score above the floor) — or the record's own `fixes` edge (`source: record`); `paths_used` on it when its source files became the scan's… |
| `tracker_namespace` | `str` | The tracker namespace bound to this code namespace that was read; "" when none is bound. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when a tracker is bound but its read failed. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |
| `partial` | `bool` | `deadline_ms` cut an optional stage: the candidates are the best found in the budget, and `partial_reason` names the stages that did not run or finish. |
| `partial_reason` | `str` |  |
| `before` | `str` | The time window the scan ran under, when no release versions bounded it ("" otherwise). |
| `after` | `str` | The window's lower bound (ISO-8601 UTC); "" when releases bounded the scan or no lower bound was given. |

## `code.blame_range`

Which merged PRs last touched these lines, between release A and B?

`POST /v1/code.blame_range` · MCP `loom_code_blame_range` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `path` | `str` | required | The repo-relative file to blame (a leading `/` is stripped). |
| `start_line` | `int` | required | First line of the range, 1-based, at the window's upper end. |
| `end_line` | `int` | required | Last line, inclusive; a range over 400 lines is cut to 400 from `start_line`. |
| `from_version` | `str` | `''` | Window start as a release (`26.3` or a full tag version); "" with no `from_sha` = the oldest release cut. |
| `to_version` | `str` | `''` | Window end as a release; "" with no `to_sha` = this namespace's head. |
| `from_sha` | `str` | `''` | Window start as a commit sha; give a version or a sha, not both. |
| `to_sha` | `str` | `''` | Window end as a commit sha; give a version or a sha, not both. |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many candidates (1–25). |
| `reviews_per_pr` | `int` | `3` | review comments per candidate inside the range (0 = none) |
| `stage` | `Literal['introduced', 'last_touched']` | `'introduced'` | introduced: rank toward the change that introduced the behaviour; last_touched: the blame order only |
| `mentions` | `str` | `''` | what misbehaves, in words: a candidate whose linked issue or title names them ranks first |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `str` | candidates \| no_candidates \| unknown \| introduced_unknown (stage introduced: blame saw no in-window line; the list is the file-touching fallback) |
| `causes` | `list[str]` | window_unresolved \| path_not_indexed \| blame_failed \| ledger_failed \| tracker_unavailable |
| `epistemic` | `str` | exact when the blame leg ran (line attribution), lower_bound when only the ledger answered (file-level) or the introduced stage is blameless |
| `stage` | `Literal['introduced', 'last_touched']` | the order `candidates` is in |
| `note` | `str` | What the answer can and cannot claim (last touched, not introduced), plus lines blame could not map to a PR. |
| `path` | `str` | The path blamed, normalized. |
| `path_indexed` | `bool` | True when the code index holds the path as a live file. |
| `range` | `dict[str, Any]` | {start, end, requested_end, truncated} |
| `window` | `dict[str, Any]` | {from_ref, to_ref, from_sha, to_sha, base_sha, from_time, to_time, sources{from,to: namespace_head\|mirror_ref\|sha\|default}, error} |
| `candidates` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | ranked: {pr_number, title, author, merged_at, first_release, lines_blamed, share_of_range, touches_file, evidence blame\|ledger\|both, kind, merge_commit_sha, merge_sha_source stored\|mirror\|"", url, has_test?, caused_by?[], fixes?[]}; stage… |
| `last_touched` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | the first stage's order, always: {pr_number, rank, lines_blamed, evidence} |
| `symbol` | `dict[str, Any]` | the enclosing function of the range when the index has one: {qualified_name, start_line, end_line} |
| `latest_pr` | `int` | the newest PR among those blame named (0 when none) |
| `lines` | `dict[str, Any]` | {total, attributed, noise, outside_window, unmapped} |
| `legs` | `dict[str, Any]` | {blame{status, warm, ms, window_commits, graph_truncated}, ledger{status, skipped: [{namespace, reason: not_readable}] when the trunk is unreadable}, introduced{status ok\|skipped, ms, git_calls, demoted, promoted, blameless}} |
| `first_release_basis` | `str` | How `first_release` was derived; "" when the mirror has no branch-cut tags. |
| `tracker_namespace` | `str` | The tracker namespace bound to this code namespace; "" when none is bound. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when a tracker is bound but its read failed; the candidates stand without `has_test` / `caused_by` / `fixes`. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.calibrate`

Derive code-specific abstention thresholds from the authored probe corpus (query/positive/hard-distractor triples over the indexed repo) and persist them as this namespace's calibration.

`POST /v1/code.calibrate` · MCP `loom_code_calibrate` · role `admin` · write · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noise_floor` | `float` | Cosine below which a hit is noise: the distractors' 90th percentile plus 0.02. |
| `abstain_threshold` | `float` | Cosine below which the search abstains: `noise_floor` plus 0.05. |
| `embedder_model` | `str` | The embedding model the probes ran against; the calibration applies to it. |
| `positives` | `int` | Query/positive pairs read from the probe corpus. |
| `distractors` | `int` | Query/distractor pairs read from the probe corpus. |

## `code.callees`

What does this symbol call — forward call edges (depth<=3), tier-marked like loom_code_callers.

`POST /v1/code.callees` · MCP `loom_code_callees` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pr_files` | `dict[str, str]` | *(computed)* | Repo-relative path -> the file's full text at the PR's head, for the files the PR adds or modifies (at most 50, 1,000,000 characters each). |
| `pr_diff` | `str` | `''` | The PR's unified diff against its merge-base (at most 1,500,000 characters): its hunks say which functions the PR modifies, and its paths name the files it deletes. |
| `pr_head_sha` | `str` | `''` | The PR's head and base commits as the caller knows them; they label the answer (`overlay_head_sha`) and never reach git. '' = derived from the text. |
| `pr_base_sha` | `str` | `''` |  |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `name` | `str` | `''` | Bare, qualified or partly qualified name of the seed symbol, or `path:line` for the innermost function containing that line. |
| `symbol_id` | `str` | `''` | An index symbol id for the seed; wins over `name`. |
| `depth` | `int` | `1` | How many hops to walk out from the seed (1–3); 1 = direct callers / callees. |
| `max_nodes` | `int` | `200` | At most this many edges across all hops (1–500); `truncated` says when it held. |
| `min_confidence` | `float` | `0.0` | Drop parser-tier edges below this confidence. |
| `include_ambiguous` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Widen the answer from "what calls it" to "what MAY call it". |
| `candidate_min_confidence` | `float \| None` | `None` | Unset = on; candidates below `candidate_min_confidence` (default the deployment floor, 0.2) are counted in the block's note and not returned. 0 shows every site. |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | An OPEN pull request whose head the mirror holds (`refs/pull/N/head`). |
| `edge_kinds` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The edge kinds the walk follows — a subset of calls \| inherits \| overrides \| fixture_use \| reads \| writes. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `edges` | `list[CodeEdgeWire]` | The call-graph edges found, hop by hop; the far end (`from_*` for callers, `to_*` for callees) is the answer. |
| `seed_symbols` | `list[str]` | Qualified names of the definitions the walk started from; empty when refused as ambiguous. |
| `overlay` | `bool` | On the wire only when `pr_number` was given. |
| `overlay_head_sha` | `str` | The PR head commit whose post-image was parsed; "" when there is no overlay. |
| `overlay_added` | `int` | How many functions the PR adds in its parsed files. |
| `overlay_note` | `str` | Why the overlay is off: `head_not_in_mirror`, `no_merge_base` or `no_repo_entry`; "" when it is on. |
| `resolved_by` | `str` | How an over-qualified name bound when the exact form missed — `anonymous_namespace` (`(anonymous namespace)::` segments stripped) or `tail` (a namespace the definition does not carry dropped; one definition fit), or `registration` when a… |
| `ambiguous` | `bool` | A bare short name that resolves to many unrelated definitions (setColumns on 60 classes) is not walked: `ambiguous` is set, `candidates` lists the qualified names to pick from, and edges is empty. |
| `candidates` | `list[str]` | With `ambiguous`: up to 20 qualified names to pick from. |
| `dispatch_seeds` | `list[dict[str, str]]` | Virtual dispatch: when the seed is an override, calls in the code go to the BASE declaration, so its callers are included and listed here as {"symbol", "via": "overrides" \| "inherits" \| "virtual_by_name"}. |
| `note` | `str` | Plain-text notes on how the walk ran: dispatch or member folding, the ambiguity refusal, declined call sites, stale compiler-tier files; "" when none apply. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | True when the walk stopped short: `max_nodes` held or a hop's edge read hit its cap. |
| `counts_floor` | `bool` | Epistemic contract: edge counts are FLOORS, never totals. |
| `unresolved_calls` | `int` | HOW LOW the floor may be (callers direction): call sites in the fast tier's files whose callee is NAMED like the seed but which the resolver declined to bind — `unresolved` (no definition of that name in the index) or `ambiguous` (several… |
| `ambiguous_calls` | `int` | Declined call sites named like the seed with several same-named definitions, none pinned (see `unresolved_calls`). |
| `epistemic` | `str` | Epistemic envelope. |
| `causes` | `list[str]` | Why `epistemic` is `lower_bound`, from the set above; empty when it is `exact`. |
| `by_hop_counts` | `dict[int, int]` | Distinct symbols reached per hop BEFORE any slicing: {1: n, 2: m}. |
| `candidate_sites` | `CodeCandidateSitesWire \| None` | Declined call sites as ranked candidates, on request only (`include_ambiguous`). |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.context_pack`

Briefing at the START of a task, instead of exploring file by file.

`POST /v1/code.context_pack` · MCP `loom_code_context_pack` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | Indexed merged PR -> precomputed pack; 0 -> orientation map; unknown PR -> explicit abstention. ge=0 because a negative number would reach ClickHouse as a UInt32 bind and surface as a 500. |
| `task` | `str` | `''` | The change about to be made ("add a new tracker op"). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `context` | `str` | The pack as Markdown text; for `unavailable`, a short note saying the PR has no pack yet. |
| `tokens_used` | `int` | Estimated tokens of `context`. |
| `source` | `Literal['precomputed', 'task', 'orientation', 'unavailable']` | precomputed (the PR's stored pack) \| task (a briefing for `task`) \| orientation (the repository map) \| unavailable (no pack for the PR). |
| `truncated` | `bool` | True when a precomputed pack was cut to `token_budget`; false for the other sources. |
| `merge_commit_sha` | `str` | The PR's merge commit, for a precomputed pack; '' otherwise. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.conventions`

The repository's recurring maintainer checks as facts over one PR's diff: a setting added or re-defaulted without a SettingsChangesHistory entry; the same setting's docs mention; a new…

`POST /v1/code.conventions` · MCP `loom_code_conventions` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | A merged PR in the ledger: its title, labels and merge commit's diff are checked; 0 = none. |
| `head_sha` | `str` | `''` | A commit the mirror holds: the diff from its merge-base with the branch tip is checked; falls back to the ledger's merge commit when the mirror lacks it. |
| `files` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | An open PR's changed paths; with `diff` they replace any ledger file list. |
| `diff` | `str` | `''` | An open PR's unified diff; its hunks are what the rules check (with `files`). |
| `rules` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The rules to run (names from the conventions rule table); empty = every rule. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pr_number` | `int` | The PR asked about; 0 when none was named. |
| `source` | `str` | ledger \| head_sha \| supplied |
| `title` | `str` | The ledger PR's title; '' when the PR is not in the ledger or none was named. |
| `labels` | `list[str]` | The ledger PR's labels. |
| `category` | `str` | bug_fix \| improvement \| new_feature \| performance \| not_for_changelog \| build \| ci \| documentation \| backward_incompatible \| experimental \| '' |
| `category_source` | `str` | Where `category` came from: `label:<name>`, `changelog_bullet` (the PR body), or ''. |
| `merged_at` | `str` | When the ledger PR merged; '' without a ledger row. |
| `merge_commit_sha` | `str` | The ledger PR's merge commit; '' without a ledger row. |
| `head_sha` | `str` | The commit the diff was read at when `source` is head_sha; otherwise the `head_sha` sent. |
| `files_total` | `int` | Changed paths known for the change (name-status list plus the diff's files). |
| `files_in_diff` | `int` | Files whose hunks were parsed from the diff; fewer than `files_total` when it was cut. |
| `diff_bytes` | `int` | Size of the diff text read, in characters; 0 without a diff. |
| `diff_truncated` | `bool` | True when the mirror diff hit `code_conventions_diff_max_bytes` and its last file was dropped; `notes` says how many files were parsed. |
| `rules` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{rule, verdict: violated\|satisfied\|not_applicable\|unknown\|unusual, evidence: [{path, line, text, ...}], epistemic: exact\|lower_bound, note}] |
| `summary` | `dict[str, int]` | verdict -> count over `rules` |
| `control` | `dict[str, Any]` | {coverage_symbol, ok, ran}: the coverage control rule 7 depends on |
| `notes` | `list[str]` | Why part of the answer is weaker: PR not in the ledger, merged into another branch, commit not in the mirror, diff cut, supplied-diff pre-image; empty when none applies. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

`POST /v1/code.coverage_claim` · MCP `loom_code_coverage_claim` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `symbol` | `str` | `''` | The subject as a symbol name (qualified or bare) or a SQL-level function name. |
| `path` | `str` | `''` | The subject as a repository-relative source path. |
| `setting` | `str` | `''` | The subject as a setting name. |
| `limit` | `int` | `20` | At most this many `tests` rows (at most 100). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `str` | The subject as given (the one of symbol, path, setting that was set). |
| `subject_kind` | `str` | symbol \| path \| setting |
| `verdict` | `str` | covered_by \| weak_evidence \| uncovered \| unknown |
| `tests` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | {test_path, methods: [...], tier, confidence, evidence} |
| `tests_total` | `int` | Tests found before `limit` (the larger of the rows and the grep's match count). |
| `src_paths` | `list[str]` | The source files the subject lives in: the path itself, the files defining the resolved symbol (first 20), or [] for a setting. |
| `epistemic` | `str` | exact when a test names the subject or the include graph reaches it; lower_bound when only mined co-occurrence or a path convention says so |
| `strongest_tier` | `str` | The strongest evidence tier among the rows (executed \| exact_scoped \| pr_cooccurrence \| short_name_grep \| file_reference \| path_convention), '' when no test was found. |

## `code.grep`

Exact-match lookup over the indexed corpus.

`POST /v1/code.grep` · MCP `loom_code_grep` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `pattern` | `str` | required | The text to find: a literal substring, or an RE2 expression with `regex`. |
| `regex` | `bool` | `False` | True reads `pattern` as RE2; an invalid expression is a 422. |
| `case_sensitive` | `bool` | `True` | False matches `pattern` regardless of letter case. |
| `path_prefix` | `str` | `''` | Only paths under this repo-relative prefix; '' = the whole index. |
| `cursor` | `str` | `''` | Continuation (matches mode): the `next_cursor` of an earlier response to this pattern; the next page of matching lines is one point read of what the first call extracted. |
| `exclude_unit_ids` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The caller's seen-set. |
| `mode` | `Literal['matches', 'files', 'presence', 'message']` | `'matches'` | matches: up to `limit` matching LINES with text + enclosing scope. files: up to `limit` matching FILES (path, matching chunk count, first line) and no line text — the coverage question ("which files mention X?") that a 20-line cap cannot… |
| `limit` | `int \| None` | `None` | Default depends on mode: 20 lines, or the 500-file ceiling — a files answer capped at 20 reads like a complete coverage answer to a caller that did not know to send a limit. matches mode is clamped to 200 lines. |
| `path_globs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | File filters, rg `-g` / `-t` style: keep paths matching any glob, drop paths matching any exclude, restrict to a language's extension set. |
| `exclude_globs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Drop paths matching any of these rg-style globs. |
| `langs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Keep only files with these languages' extensions (rg `-t` names: cpp, py, ts, go, …); an unknown name is a 422 that lists the known ones. |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Several namespaces, mode="presence" only: at most 8, trimmed, duplicates removed; `namespace`, when set and absent, leads the list. |
| `neighbours` | `bool \| None` | `None` | The neighbours graph block in the SAME call, matches mode only: the hits' enclosing functions become anchors (at most 20, first appearance) and each carries up to `neighbour_k` callers, callees and mapped tests at edge confidence >= 0.8… |
| `neighbour_k` | `int` | `5` | With `neighbours`: at most this many callers and callees per anchor (1..20). |
| `deadline_ms` | `int \| None` | `None` | The request's wall-clock budget in ms, from arrival (values under 200 read as 200). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `matches` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | {path, line, text, scope, scope_start_line, scope_end_line} per matching LINE, path/line ordered. scope_* is the span of the enclosing unit named by `scope` (0/0 when the line sits in no unit) — enough to decide whether to fetch the body… |
| `next_cursor` | `str` | Continuation: cursor for the next page of matching lines, "" when the extracted set is exhausted. has_more mirrors it. |
| `has_more` | `bool` | True when `next_cursor` is set. |
| `files` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | mode=files: {path, chunks, first_line} per matching file, path ordered. |
| `files_total` | `int` | distinct matching files before `limit` (mode=files) |
| `chunks_matched` | `int` | Indexed chunks read that contain the pattern (matches mode over-fetches up to 200). |
| `truncated` | `bool` | True when more lines or files match than were returned, or the chunk read hit its cap. |
| `coverage_floor` | `bool` | Chunk coverage is not byte-complete for a file: absence here cannot prove absence in the repo (same floor contract as code.verify). |
| `as_of` | `dict[str, Any]` | Provenance + freshness: branch, commit, indexed_at, lag_commits (int, -1 unknown), stale (bool: lag > LOOM_CODE_STALE_AFTER_COMMITS). |
| `not_covered` | `bool` | True when path_prefix lies outside the indexed prefixes (hits are then empty by construction, not by absence). |
| `neighbours` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | The neighbours graph block: one entry per anchor — symbol_id, qualified_name, path, module, callers, callees, tests, epistemic, causes; empty unless `neighbours` ran. |
| `anchors` | `int` | distinct enclosing functions the block covers |
| `anchors_capped` | `bool` | more resolved functions than the 20 cap |
| `neighbour_tokens` | `int` | Tokens of the neighbours block alone; 0 when it did not run. |
| `note` | `str` | A caveat on the answer: the pattern was re-read as a regex or matched literally, the prefix is outside the index, or the embedding coverage is low; '' when none. |
| `verdict` | `str` | mode=message only (dropped from the wire otherwise): raised_at \| no_template_match; the message's `{}` template; the ErrorCodes name for a `Code: N` prefix ("" when unmapped); the best statement's coverage (matched message characters /… |
| `template` | `str` | mode=message: the message with `{}` where arguments stood. |
| `error_code` | `str` | mode=message: the ErrorCodes name for a `Code: N` prefix; '' when unmapped. |
| `coverage` | `float` | mode=message: the best statement's matched share of the message characters (0..1). |
| `presence` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | mode=presence: one row per requested namespace, in request order — {namespace, verdict: present \| absent \| unknown, path, start_line, end_line, tier: "", files_total, indexed_commit, index_status, ms, reason}. |
| `summary` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | mode=presence: {present, absent, unknown}, each the namespaces with that verdict. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row ('' on a not_covered answer); pass it to `code.outcome`. |
| `partial` | `bool` | `deadline_ms` stopped the scan (or skipped a later read): the hits are those found in the budget and `partial_reason` says what was cut. |
| `partial_reason` | `str` | What the deadline cut, as `deadline N ms: <stage>; <stage>`. |
| `fallback` | `Literal['', 'literal']` | mode=message whose pattern matched no statement template: "literal" when the same pattern was then run as a plain matches grep and `matches` are its lines (the verdict fields stay the message read's). |

| `profile` | `str` |  |
| `compiler_candidates` | `list[str]` | Compiler tiers inferred from the indexed tree, even before a compiler worker has produced its first watermark. |

| `pr_cursor` | `str` | The PR-history poller's cursor: the newest `updated_at` (ISO-8601) of the merged PRs it fetched; '' before its first pass. |
| `commit_coverage` | `CodeCommitCoverage \| None` | Set when the request named a `commit`. |
| `clone_head` | `str` | Freshness. clone_head is the bare clone's branch tip as of the last poller fetch (<= interval old); *_lag = first-parent commits between a watermark and that tip, -1 when a watermark is unset or the clone is unreadable. 0 everywhere ==… |
| `clone_fetched_at` | `str` | When the ingest pass last fetched this entry's mirror (the `clone_head` row's updated_at, ISO-8601 UTC; '' unknown) and whether that is older than `code_fetch_stale_after_seconds`. |
| `fetch_overdue` | `bool` | True when `clone_fetched_at` is older than `code_fetch_stale_after_seconds`. |
| `fast_tier_lag` | `int` | First-parent commits between `git_head` and `clone_head`; -1 when either is unknown. |
| `scip_lag` | `int` | First-parent commits between `scip_commit` and `clone_head`; -1 when either is unknown. |
| `scip_py_lag` | `int` | First-parent commits between `scip_commit_py` and `clone_head`; -1 when either is unknown. |
| `last_refresh_at` | `str` | Last code.refresh request (the CI hook). |
| `last_refresh_detail` | `str` | The caller of that request, as `agent=<agent> expected_head=<first 12 hex>`; a field the caller left empty is left out. |
| `org_readable` | `bool` | Deployment-level read rule (LOOM_CODE_ORG_READABLE / per-entry): when true every org principal reads this entry regardless of visibility. |
| `path_prefixes` | `list[str]` | The path prefixes the entry indexes; `[""]` = the whole tree. |
| `counts` | `dict[str, int]` | Live row counts per code table (`code_files`, `code_chunks`, `code_symbols`, …); empty in the brief answer. |

| `workers` | `dict[str, CodeWorkerStatus]` | Per `code_*` worker, its enabled flag, interval and last pass; empty in the brief answer. |
| `build_commit` | `str` | Capability catalogue: the build this server runs and every served code.* operation with the request fields its input model accepts, so a client checks for a route or a field instead of probing for a 404 or a 422. |
| `ops` | `list[str]` | Every served `code.*` operation, sorted; empty in the brief answer. |
| `request_fields` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | Per served op, the request fields its input model accepts; empty in the brief answer. |
| `op_maturity` | `dict[str, str]` | Per served op, its maturity (stable \| experimental) and the reach kinds a caller has to it. |
| `op_reach` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | Per served op, its reach kinds (mcp_core \| mcp_atomic \| mcp_all \| sdk_method \| sdk_example \| plugin_hook \| dashboard \| http_only); empty in the brief answer. |
| `op_toolsets` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | Per served op, every MCP toolset whose listing carries it (core \| coding \| atomic \| all; empty when hidden). |
| `symbol_stats_rows` | `int` | The weekly symbol fan-in table for this namespace — live rows with callers and the newest pass stamp (ISO 8601, UTC). 0 / "" = the pass has not written it: every `fan_in` field, the fan-in sort and the rank prior answer empty. |
| `symbol_stats_at` | `str` | The newest fan-in pass stamp (ISO-8601 UTC); '' when the pass has not written the table. |
| `unit_risk_rows` | `int` | The precomputed risk table for this namespace — live rows and the newest stamp (ISO 8601, UTC), so an operator sees the weekly leg's progress and a resumed pass's remainder. 0 / "" = no row written (every served unit is read live). |
| `unit_risk_at` | `str` | The newest risk-table stamp (ISO-8601 UTC); '' when no row is written. |
| `chunks_total` | `int` | Live chunks, those carrying a vector, and their ratio (0..1; reference fixtures unembedded by design are outside the denominator). |
| `chunks_embedded` | `int` | Live chunks that carry an embedding vector. |
| `embedding_coverage` | `float` | Embedded share of the embeddable chunks (0..1); 1.0 when the counts do not carry it. |

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `action` | `Literal['opened_file', 'used_in_answer', 'fell_back_grep', 'ignored', 'shunt_hit', 'shunt_pass']` | required | What happened after the answer: opened_file (a returned file was read), used_in_answer, fell_back_grep, ignored; or a batch of shunt-hook decisions (shunt_hit \| shunt_pass). |

| `spans` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Aligned with `targets`: the line span each decision / open covered, as `path:start-end` (shunt rows: the file and the lines the Read would cover), `start-end` (opened_file: the Read's offset/limit against the target path) or '' when… |
| `reason` | `str` | `''` | fell_back_grep / ignored: WHY, from OUTCOME_REASONS. |

## `code.outline`

"What is in this file?" — the question a whole-file read answers at the price of the whole file.

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `path` | `str` | required | repo-relative path ("src/Foo.cpp"); a leading ./ is tolerated |

| `as_of` | `dict[str, Any]` | Provenance + freshness: branch, commit, indexed_at, lag_commits (int, -1 unknown), stale (bool: lag > LOOM_CODE_STALE_AFTER_COMMITS). |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.path_guards`

The conditions that stand on the call path from `from_symbol` to `to_symbol`: the verify(reaches) chain, and for each hop the guards the call site sits under inside its caller…

`POST /v1/code.path_guards` · MCP `loom_code_path_guards` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `from_symbol` | `str` | required | The symbol the call path starts from. |
| `to_symbol` | `str` | required | a symbol name, or a path prefix (contains '/') like verify(reaches) |
| `mentions` | `str` | `''` | the identifier the question asks about ('' lists the guards only) |
| `depth` | `int` | `4` | The most call hops the walk follows (1..4). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `Literal['guarded_by', 'no_guard_named', 'path_found', 'path_not_found', 'unknown']` | guarded_by a guard on some hop names `mentions` no_guard_named the path was found, no guard on it names `mentions` path_found the path was found and `mentions` was empty (listing) path_not_found the bounded walk emptied its frontier… |
| `causes` | `list[str]` | Machine-readable causes behind `unknown`, and the standing floors of a syntactic read otherwise (empty on guarded_by/no_guard_named/path_found only when nothing further limited the answer). |
| `epistemic` | `Literal['lower_bound']` | Always `lower_bound`: guards are read syntactically inside each caller only. |
| `explanation` | `str` | A human-readable account of how the verdict was reached. |
| `hops` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | One entry per hop, seed first. |
| `named_at` | `list[str]` | The hops whose guards name `mentions`, as "path:line" — the places to read |
| `visited_symbols` | `int` | Symbols the bounded call walk visited. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.repo.add`

Add a repository's branch as a new read-only index.

`POST /v1/code.repo.add` · MCP `loom_code_repo_add` · role `viewer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `repo` | `str` | required | GitHub owner/name or an HTTPS/SSH Git URL. |
| `branch` | `str` | `''` | Blank asks the remote for its symbolic default branch. |
| `join_policy` | `Literal['open', 'approval']` | `'open'` | `open`: any org member joins at once; `approval`: a maintainer approves each request. |
| `classification` | `Literal['standard', 'restricted']` | `'standard'` | `standard` or `restricted` (a reader needs an approved grant and a token that names the namespace). |
| `access_token` | `str` | `''` | Token for a private HTTPS remote; stored encrypted, never returned. |
| `path_prefixes` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Path prefixes to index (`src/`, `lib/`); blank entries are dropped, [] indexes the whole tree. |
| `exclude` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Globs never indexed for this repository (`vendor/`, `*.generated.go`); [] keeps the deployment's default exclude list. |
| `exclude_generated` | `bool` | `True` | Refuse generated content (Go's `// Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.` header, the `@generated` marker, the repository's `.gitattributes` linguist rules) — on unless the maintainer says otherwise |
| `scip_producer` | `Literal['', 'go', 'typescript', 'clang', 'python']` | `''` | The compiler tier's producer; "" infers it from the tree's manifests (go.mod → go, tsconfig / package.json → typescript, a root CMakeLists.txt → clang, pyproject → python) |

| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |

| `sections` | `list[Literal['paths', 'symbols', 'tests', 'settings', 'history', 'blame', 'qa', 'risk', 'do_not_flag', 'rationale']]` | *(computed)* | Serve only these of the tier's sections; empty = every section the tier carries. |

| `ledger` | `Literal['', 'present', 'absent']` | what the ledger said: present (this build read its row) \| absent (this or the stored build came from the mirror because the ledger had no row) \| "" (not consulted: the ingest built the row) |

| `sections` | `dict[str, dict[str, Any]]` | name -> {status, verdict, epistemic, causes, rows, rows_total, tokens, truncated} |

## `code.search`

Search the shared code index of this repository (fresh to the last merged PR).

`POST /v1/code.search` · MCP `loom_code_search` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `query` | `str` | required | The question, identifier or phrase to search for; a symbol-shaped query tries the symbol table first (`route` says which path answered). |
| `top_k` | `int` | `5` | At most this many results per page (1-25). |
| `token_budget` | `int \| None` | `None` | Response budget in tokens; results are whole units, overflow elides. |
| `path_prefix` | `str` | `''` | Keep only units whose path starts with this prefix; "" = the whole namespace. |
| `cursor` | `str` | `''` | Continuation: the `next_cursor` of an earlier response to this query. |
| `exclude_unit_ids` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The caller's seen-set: unit ids not to serve again. |
| `rerank` | `str` | `''` | Reranker over the fused pool: "" = the deployment default (LOOM_CODE_SEARCH_RERANK_DEFAULT, for prose questions of its kinds), "none" = off for this request, "builtin:openai" / "builtin:cohere", or the name of an endpoint in… |
| `expand` | `bool` | `False` | Vocabulary bridge: one LLM hop proposes codebase identifiers for the lexical leg (natural-language wording often misses the implementing subsystem's vocabulary). |
| `annotate` | `bool` | `True` | Risk annotations + one-hop callee context per result (churn/amp/tested/ callees on each unit). |
| `bodies` | `Literal['auto', 'none'] \| None` | `None` | "auto" (default): granularity scales with budget-per-slot — cards when the budget can't fit any body (~<200 tok/slot), whole units in the normal range, and top hits expand toward their WHOLE FILE when the budget is generous. "none": cards… |
| `kind_prior` | `Literal['off', 'default', 'flat', 'structural'] \| None` | `None` | Chunk-kind prior override for A/B: None = the served "flat" table; "default" / "flat" pick a table, "structural" applies only the phrasing rule, "off" disables. |
| `pr_leg_before` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Only PRs merged strictly before this instant may vote — the time-travel pin a bench mined from merged PRs needs so the fix PR cannot vote for its own files. |
| `embedding_model` | `str` | `''` | Bench-only override of the embedding_model label the legs read: "" = the deployment embedder's model name. |
| `fresh` | `bool` | `False` | true = bypass the served-response memo and compute. |
| `min_fan_in` | `int` | `0` | Symbol fan-in (loom.code_symbol_stats, weekly). |
| `sort_by` | `Literal['score', 'fan_in']` | `'score'` | "score" = ranked relevance order; "fan_in" = order the pool by `fan_in`, most-called first. |
| `pattern` | `str` | `''` | Constrained search: a literal (default) or RE2 regex that every returned chunk must contain — applied to BOTH legs' pools before ranking, so one call replaces grep-then-search. |
| `regex` | `bool` | `False` | true = `pattern` is an RE2 regex (an invalid one is a 422); false = a literal substring. |
| `case_sensitive` | `bool` | `False` | true = `pattern` matches case-sensitively; false (default) ignores case. |
| `path_globs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Indexed-route file filters, rg `-g` / `-t` style: keep paths matching any glob (`*.cpp`, `src/Parsers/`), drop paths matching any exclude, restrict to a language's extension set (cpp, python, sql, ...). |
| `exclude_globs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Drop paths matching any of these globs (same syntax as path_globs); at most 8. |
| `langs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Keep only files of these languages by extension (cpp, c, python/py, js, ts, go, rust, java, sql, md, ...); an unknown name is a 422 listing the known ones. |
| `legs` | `Literal['hybrid', 'lexical', 'vector'] \| None` | `None` | Leg ablation for A/B: None/"hybrid" = both legs; "lexical" skips the vector leg AND the embedding call; "vector" skips the lexical leg. |
| `track_path` | `str` | `''` | Developer diagnostic, not exposed to the shunt: the path of the file the caller EXPECTED to see. |
| `vector_model` | `str` | `''` | Second vector model: the spec of an embedder the deployment lists in LOOM_CODE_SEARCH_VECTOR_MODELS. |
| `vector_shortlist` | `int \| None` | `None` | With vector_model set: > 0 = the second model shortlists this many chunk ids and the served model's vectors rescore them exactly; 0 = the second model's own distances rank the pool; None = the deployment's code_search_vector_shortlist. |
| `llm_legs` | `Literal['auto', 'none'] \| None` | `None` | `none` skips the model-backed legs — HyDE (an LLM passage, a second embed and a full scan) and a model-named concept source; `auto` (None = the deployment default, LOOM_CODE_SEARCH_LLM_LEGS_DEFAULT) runs what the deployment configures. |
| `deadline_ms` | `int \| None` | `None` | The request's wall-clock budget in ms, from arrival (values under 200 read as 200). |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Several namespaces at once: the single-namespace search runs once per entry, concurrently, and the rankings are interleaved by RANK in this order — scores are not comparable across namespaces (the lexical idf is per namespace). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `list[CodeUnit]` | The ranked units served on this page, cut to top_k and the token budget; empty on an abstain with no pool or a not-covered path. |
| `route` | `str` | symbol_exact \| hybrid \| symbol_miss_hybrid |
| `next_cursor` | `str` | Continuation: opaque cursor for the next page of the ranked pool, "" when nothing ranked remains past this page (symbol routes issue none). has_more mirrors it. |
| `has_more` | `bool` | true when `next_cursor` is set, i.e. more ranked results remain past this page. |
| `history` | `dict[str, Any]` | History section: {intent: number\|phrase, numbers, items: [{number, kind, state, title, ...}], prs: [{pr_number, title, author, merged_at, files, files_total, role}], anchored: [{path, placed}], tokens}. |
| `abstain` | `bool` | true = the server does not stand behind these results (they may still be listed); `abstain_code` says why. |
| `abstain_code` | `Literal['', 'no_match', 'below_threshold', 'low_calibrated_confidence', 'not_covered', 'pattern_too_broad', 'identifier_absent', 'off_domain']` | Why it abstained: no_match (nothing survived) \| below_threshold (top cosine under the abstain threshold) \| low_calibrated_confidence \| not_covered (path outside the index) \| pattern_too_broad \| identifier_absent (no file names it) \|… |
| `abstain_reason` | `str` | Human-readable reason for the abstain, with what to do instead; "" when not abstaining. |
| `retrieval_risk` | `Literal['low', 'medium', 'high', 'abstain']` | Calibrated risk band from `retrieval_confidence`: low (>= 0.75), medium (>= 0.55), high, or abstain (below the abstain cut-off or the top cosine under its threshold). |
| `retrieval_confidence` | `float` | Calibrated confidence 0-1 from the top similarity, its margin over the second hit, `route_agreement` and the pool size; 0.0 on an abstain with no results. |
| `route_agreement` | `float` | Share (0-1) of the retrieval routes that ran and agreed: the primary hit, lexical and vector legs sharing a top-10 chunk, a fuzzy-symbol hit; 1.0 on an exact symbol hit. |
| `calibration_explanation` | `str` | The calibration inputs as text (top_similarity, margin, route_agreement, ...), plus the legs the answer ranked without past the deadline. |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated tokens of the served page (results, history section and annotations). |
| `constrained` | `bool` | Constrained search: true when a pattern / path filter narrowed the pool; `matched_files` is the pre-count of files the constraint admits (0 when unconstrained or not counted). |
| `matched_files` | `int` | How many files the pattern / path constraint admits; 0 when unconstrained or not counted. |
| `as_of` | `dict[str, Any]` | Provenance + freshness: branch, commit, indexed_at, lag_commits (int, -1 unknown), stale (bool: lag > LOOM_CODE_STALE_AFTER_COMMITS). |
| `score_explanation` | `str` | How the answer was reached as text: fusion kind and leg row counts, legs agreement, the constraint and matched_files, priors and history votes that applied. |
| `retrieval_work` | `dict[str, int \| str]` | Counters per stage, plus `risk_source` — "table" \| "live" \| "mixed": where the served risk block came from when the precomputed table is on. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of the loom.code_search_trace row the server writes for this call. |
| `top_similarity` | `float` | Raw cosine of the top vector-leg hit (0.0 when the vector leg did not run or the route was symbol_exact). |
| `tracked` | `dict[str, Any]` | track_path diagnostic: {path, verdict, chunks, pool, best: {chunk_id, scope, start_line, lexical_rank, vector_rank, lex_score, distance, served_rank}, lexical_floor, vector_ceiling}. |
| `fanout` | `dict[str, Any]` | Fan-out disclosure: {namespaces, interleave: "rank", timeout_ms, per_namespace: {ns: {ms, results, abstain, route, commit, trace_run_id}}, dropped: [ns...]}. |
| `note` | `str` | e.g. "lexical only until embeddings finish (41% embedded)" while the namespace's vector leg covers less than LOOM_CODE_READY_EMBED_COVERAGE of its chunks (a first index still embedding, a backfill without --embed); "" otherwise. |
| `legs_timed_out` | `list[str]` | The legs the deadline (or the model-leg grace) dropped — their rows are not in the ranking — and `epistemic` "partial" then, or when a content leg failed (`retrieval_work` names it). |
| `epistemic` | `Literal['', 'partial']` | "partial" when a leg timed out or a content leg failed; off the wire otherwise. |
| `partial` | `bool` | `deadline_ms` cut something (a leg, rerank, a late stage): the page is the best found in the budget, and `partial_reason` names what did not finish. |
| `partial_reason` | `str` | What the deadline cut, as `deadline N ms: <stage>; <stage>`; off the wire otherwise. |

## `code.symbol`

Exact symbol lookup: definition, signature, doc comment, and body of a function/class/enum by (qualified) name — compiler-grade where available (tier='scip'), resolved across C++ overloads…

`POST /v1/code.symbol` · MCP `loom_code_symbol` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `name` | `str` | `''` | bare, qualified, or partially qualified name — or `path:line` ("src/Foo.cpp:123"), which resolves to the innermost function containing that line: a grep hit or review comment becomes the whole function in one call. |
| `symbol_id` | `str` | `''` | An index symbol id (a definition's `unit_id`, an edge's `*_symbol_id`); when set it wins over `name` and resolves exactly that definition. |
| `include_body` | `bool` | `True` | Read each definition's body; a 200+ line class ships its skeleton plus member outline instead. |
| `include_history` | `bool` | `True` | Attach `recent_prs` (merged PRs over the definitions' paths) to the first definition. |
| `include_examples` | `bool` | `True` | Attach `examples` (call sites that use the symbol) to the first definition. |
| `include_lessons` | `bool` | `True` | Attach `lessons` to the first definition: the memories linked to the symbol from `lesson_namespaces` (over MCP the caller's memory home by default) and the repository's team namespace, each with its `code_state` (`fresh`, `moved`, or… |
| `lesson_namespaces` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The memory namespaces whose linked memories `lessons` reads besides the repository's team rules (over MCP the caller's memory home by default); one the caller cannot read is skipped. |
| `token_budget` | `int` | `2500` | Estimated-token budget for the answer; definitions past it are served elided (signature, doc, pointer), and the `uses_brief` block is paid out of it first. |
| `min_fan_in` | `int` | `0` | Definitions carry `fan_in` when the weekly stats are enabled; min_fan_in drops the rest, sort_by='fan_in' puts the most-called definition of an overloaded/ambiguous name first. |
| `sort_by` | `Literal['score', 'fan_in']` | `'score'` | `score` keeps the resolver's order; `fan_in` puts the most-called definition first. |
| `uses` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `uses=true` returns the definition AND the lines that mention its bare name — what a separate code.grep on the name would return, read beside the definition from the same chunk index — minus the definition's own span(s). |
| `uses_limit` | `int` | `50` | At most this many `uses` lines (1–200) when `uses` is true. |
| `uses_brief` | `bool` | `False` | Serve the compact `uses` block when the lookup resolves to one definition; ignored when `uses` is true. |
| `near_paths` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | When several definitions match, rank them by the change at hand — the files in `near_paths` (<= 20) or the merged PR's file list for `pr_number` from the ledger: same file, same directory, co-change in code_pr_history, then path distance. |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | A merged PR whose file list (from the PR ledger) ranks several matching definitions; 0 = no PR ranking. |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Presence on several namespaces: `presence: true` runs the resolve once per entry of `namespaces` (at most 8; `namespace`, when set and absent, leads the list; unset list = the addressed namespace alone), concurrently under… |
| `presence` | `bool` | `False` | Answer per namespace in `namespaces` whether the definition is there (the `presence` / `summary` blocks) instead of returning definitions. |
| `neighbours` | `bool \| None` | `None` | The neighbours graph block for the resolved definitions themselves — k callers, callees, tests and citing documents per definition, in the same call. |
| `neighbour_k` | `int` | `5` | How many callers, callees, tests and citing documents (each) the `neighbours` block lists per definition. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `definitions` | `list[CodeUnit]` | The resolved definitions (at most 10), fitted to `token_budget`; empty when nothing resolved (see `candidates`) or on a presence answer. |
| `ambiguous` | `bool` | True when the served definitions carry more than one distinct name/signature pair. |
| `hierarchy` | `dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]` | For a class / interface / enum definition, its type hierarchy from the `inherits` edges of both tiers, folded by qualified name: {"supertypes": [...], "subtypes": [...]} of {symbol, kind, via (extends \| implements), tier, confidence… |
| `candidates` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | When nothing resolved: cheap fuzzy candidates (names + paths only). |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated tokens of the answer: definitions, uses, cited documents, neighbours and hierarchy blocks together. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |
| `uses` | `list[dict[str, Any]] \| dict[str, Any]` | uses=true: {path, line, text, scope, scope_start_line, scope_end_line, kind} per line mentioning the symbol's bare name, path/line ordered, the definition span(s) excluded. |
| `uses_truncated` | `bool` | True when the `uses` list stopped at `uses_limit`. |
| `uses_tokens` | `int` | Estimated tokens the compact `uses` block cost out of `token_budget`. |
| `picked_by` | `str` | Which context key ranked the definitions when `near_paths` / `pr_number` was given — same_file \| same_dir \| co_change \| path_distance \| none. "" and off the wire when no context was given. |
| `resolved_by` | `str` | `anonymous_namespace` \| `tail` when an over-qualified name bound through symbol-form tolerance; "" and off the wire otherwise. |
| `documented_in` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | The document sections that cite the definition (the Markdown lane's `reads` edges) — section qualified name, path, line; at most five distinct sections, first by confidence. |
| `neighbours` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | The neighbours graph block on the definitions (one entry per definition anchor); empty unless `neighbours` ran. |
| `anchors` | `int` | How many definitions the `neighbours` block was built for; 0 when it is off. |
| `neighbour_tokens` | `int` | Estimated tokens the `neighbours` block cost (counted in `tokens_returned`). |
| `presence` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | presence=true: one row per requested namespace, in request order — {namespace, verdict: present \| absent \| unknown, path, start_line, end_line, tier, indexed_commit, index_status, ms, reason, definitions}. |
| `summary` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | Presence summary: {present, absent, unknown} lists of namespaces; also filled from the entry's `depends_on` namespaces when the name is not defined here. |

| `causes` | `list[str]` | Why `epistemic` is lower_bound (values above); [] when it is exact. |
| `by_hop_counts` | `dict[int, int]` | Distinct symbols reached per hop BEFORE any slicing: {1: n, 2: m}. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's row in `loom.code_search_trace`. |
