## `code.trace`

Paste a stack trace / backtrace; get each frame resolved to its definition in one call — the incident-workflow entry point.

`POST /v1/code.trace` · MCP `loom_code_trace` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `trace` | `str` | required | The stack trace or backtrace text; qualified `a::b` names and C/C++ `dir/file.cpp:N` locations are read as frames (`std::`, `boost::`, `absl::`, `__*` frames skipped). |
| `max_frames` | `int` | `15` | Resolve at most this many distinct frames, in trace order (1..40). |
| `token_budget` | `int` | `3000` | Token budget for `definitions` (200..12000); units past it are dropped. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frames` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | One entry per recognized frame, trace order: {frame, qualified_name, path, line, symbol_id, resolved}. |
| `definitions` | `list[CodeUnit]` | The resolved definitions, whole units within `token_budget`. |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated tokens of `definitions`. |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.verify`

Verify one closed-form claim against the index and return a three-valued verdict.

`POST /v1/code.verify` · MCP `loom_code_verify` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `kind` | `Literal['calls', 'unused', 'defines', 'contains', 'reaches']` | required | The claim's shape: calls \| unused \| defines \| contains \| reaches (see above). |
| `subject` | `str` | required | What the claim is about: a symbol name, or a repo-relative path for defines/contains. |
| `object` | `str` | `''` | The claim's other end: a symbol, a literal (contains) or a path prefix (reaches); '' for unused. |
| `depth` | `int` | `4` | For calls and reaches: the most call hops the walk follows (1..6). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `Literal['confirmed', 'refuted', 'not_established']` | A subject or object that resolves no symbol is a RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND refusal, not a verdict; its detail carries `role` (subject \| object) and `did_you_mean`, up to 5 of code.symbol's near misses {qualified_name, path, kind, tier… |
| `reason` | `str` | Machine-readable cause, stable for bots to branch on. |
| `explanation` | `str` | A human-readable account of how the verdict was reached. |
| `evidence` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | Positive rows behind the verdict: edges (a call chain, in order), symbol rows, or content excerpts — shape depends on kind. |
| `floors` | `dict[str, Any]` | Why refutation was unavailable when the verdict is not_established: what was searched, how far, and which blind spots apply. |
| `index_verdict` | `str` | The index's own verdict behind a `not_established` claim ('' otherwise). |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |

## `code.verify_citations`

Every citation a draft carries, resolved against the index before the draft is posted somewhere public and irreversible.

`POST /v1/code.verify_citations` · MCP `loom_code_verify_citations` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pr_files` | `dict[str, str]` | *(computed)* | Repo-relative path -> the file's full text at the PR's head, for the files the PR adds or modifies (at most 50, 1,000,000 characters each). |
| `pr_diff` | `str` | `''` | The PR's unified diff against its merge-base (at most 1,500,000 characters): its hunks say which functions the PR modifies, and its paths name the files it deletes. |
| `pr_head_sha` | `str` | `''` | The PR's head and base commits as the caller knows them; they label the answer (`overlay_head_sha`) and never reach git. '' = derived from the text. |
| `pr_base_sha` | `str` | `''` |  |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `consumer` | `str` | `''` | trace attribution: which integration is calling (clickgap\|claude-code\|…) |
| `text` | `str` | required | The draft to check: a review comment, PR body or answer, as plain text or Markdown. |
| `at_commit` | `str` | `''` | The commit the draft was written against; '' = check against the index head only (or the PR's merge commit with `pr_number`). |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | The reviewed PR; 0 = no PR-diff leg |
| `base_namespace` | `str` | `''` | Namespace read after the addressed one for citations it did not resolve; '' = the mirror's default-branch entry when the addressed one is a release branch. |
| `limit` | `int` | `200` | citations verified per call, first-appearance order; the rest are counted in `truncated` |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `str` | all_resolved \| has_unresolved \| has_stale \| no_citations. |
| `counts` | `dict[str, int]` | total, resolved, unresolved, stale, ambiguous, kind_<kind> counts |
| `citations` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | one per distinct citation, first-appearance order: {kind, text, verdict, reason, epistemic, occurrences, path?, start_line?, end_line?, number?, name?, rev?, form?, in_pr_diff?, in_code_block?, target?, candidates?}. form: basename \|… |
| `skipped` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | names not verified because their outermost scope is an external library (std::, boost::, …): {kind, text, reason} |
| `truncated` | `bool` | True when the draft held more distinct citations than `limit`; the rest are unchecked. |
| `epistemic` | `dict[str, str]` | per check: path / number / name / commit -> exact; line -> lower_bound |
| `at_commit` | `dict[str, Any]` | {requested, sha, known, calls, capped, ms, error} — the mirror leg |
| `pr_diff` | `dict[str, Any]` | only with `pr_number`: {pr_number, merge_sha, source: ledger \| mirror_log \| "", files_in_diff, in_diff, off_diff, unknown, calls, ms, error: "" \| pr_unknown \| log_failed \| diff_failed \| hunks_failed} |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | The namespaces read, in order: the addressed one, then the base one if any. |
| `took_ms` | `int` | Server-side wall time of the call, in milliseconds. |
| `as_of` | `dict[str, Any]` | Provenance + freshness: branch, commit, indexed_at, lag_commits (int, -1 unknown), stale (bool: lag > LOOM_CODE_STALE_AFTER_COMMITS). |
| `note` | `str` | How far the checks can be trusted, plus why a leg was cut (unknown commit, capped mirror leg, PR not found, truncated citations). |
| `trace_run_id` | `str` | Id of this call's trace row; pass it to `code.outcome`. |
